items.summary: We present Underwater C$^{3}$-JEPA (cross-view, control-conditioned, context-extended), an object-centric multi-view predictive world model for near-field heavy-load underwater ROV salvage. Without contact sensors, it predicts in latent space how the task-object state evolves through contact interaction and under the hydrodynamic lag of the vehicle, from synchronized multi-view RGB observations and vehicle control signals. C$^{3}$-JEPA encodes multi-camera observations into task-object and context tokens, fuses cross-camera evidence through held-out-view attention, and directly predicts future states conditioned on control. Weak binding anchors the target and gripper at low annotation cost, while SIGReg sharpens the geometric representation. Experiments show that the learned representation transfers substantially more task-relevant information to downstream probes than a reconstruction-free latent baseline, while keeping the predictor lightweight. The resulting predictive interface supports model-predictive-control (MPC) candidate evaluation and imagined-rollout behavior-agent training. Validation on real underwater video shows the same architecture recovering a withheld camera's object state and staying ahead of persistence, so the recipe transfers beyond simulation.
items.title: Underwater C3-JEPA: An Object-Centric Cross-View World Model for ROV Salvage

items.summary: Planners built on visual world models commonly score each predicted outcome by its distance to the encoded goal image. We show that this target can limit control even with exact dynamics and globally optimal short-horizon search: reaching a goal may require actions that initially move away from it. With frozen LeWM models, intermediate targets substantially improve action synthesis and recorded-action ranking on Cube, PushT, Reacher, and TwoRoom. Learned targets and targets drawn from observed experience both produce these gains. We introduce Anchored Planning, which retrieves a recorded segment whose start and end resemble the current and goal observations, then aims at an observation shortly after its start. The frozen model scores actions toward this target from the current state. Without additional training, planning toward observed targets outperforms the released LeWM planner on every task in our long-range evaluation. Additional final-goal search falls short of the same gains. Lower successor-prediction error need not translate into better control. Success also depends on how far ahead the target is placed and on shrinking the retrieval span as execution advances. Changing only the target lets the same frozen model and planner reach goals that final-goal scoring misses.
items.title: Aim Short to Reach Far: Your Frozen World Model Can Plan Better Than You Think

items.summary: Latent world models are typically trained to predict factual transitions, whereas model predictive control (MPC) must compare alternative actions from the same state. A model can therefore achieve low factual prediction error yet poorly distinguish candidate actions. We introduce AD-WM, an action-discriminative joint-embedding world model for counterfactual MPC. AD-WM combines residual latent dynamics with predictor-level action-recovery regularization, using inverse dynamics and a normalized recovery objective motivated by conditional mutual information. Both objectives encourage planning transitions to preserve action information; their auxiliary heads are discarded at test time, leaving MPC unchanged. On OGBench-Cube, AD-WM improves hard-start success from 3.7% to 52.0% over a matched LeWM baseline and improves mean success over the reproduced baseline in four of five simulation environments. Planning diagnostics show that factual prediction error and whole-bank action ranking do not follow the closed-loop success ordering, whereas CEM-aligned elite regret tracks success more closely. With a frozen V-JEPA 2 encoder and matched DROID post-training, AD-WM also improves zero-shot transfer to our Franka setup, increasing basic pick-and-place success from 42.2% to 71.1% without lab-specific adaptation. These results suggest that world models for planning should preserve action-dependent differences needed for counterfactual selection, rather than optimize factual prediction accuracy alone. More videos and code are available at https://ad-wm.github.io/.
items.title: AD-WM: Action-Discriminative World Models for Counterfactual Model Predictive Control

items.summary: Latent neural surrogate solvers, or latent dynamics models, accelerate simulations of time-dependent physical systems by evolving a compressed latent space rather than resolving full-resolution fields directly. In principle this reduces computational cost and simplifies learning, but in practice errors often accumulate rapidly during long autoregressive rollouts, limiting predictive utility. We show that this instability does not stem from the latent representation itself, but arises when it is trained solely for reconstruction, producing representations poorly suited to long-horizon forecasting. We systematically evaluate training-level interventions that align latent representations with long-horizon rollout: Koopman operator learning and Hamming noise injection during autoencoder training to improve compression, together with noise injection and multi-step rollout fine-tuning to improve dynamics. Interventions that improve long-horizon rollout stability often degrade conventional training metrics, including reconstruction and one-step prediction accuracy. Collectively, these interventions reduce long-rollout error by approximately 40\% and match or exceed the accuracy of full-resolution models on two physics benchmarks, while requiring 2 orders of magnitude fewer floating point operations and half the GPU memory. Applied to mesoscale crystal-plasticity simulations of high-cycle fatigue, the resulting surrogate achieves stable extrapolation over horizons orders of magnitude beyond those observed during training. More broadly, these results show that neural compression should be designed not merely to reduce dimensionality, but to restructure the solution space for stable dynamical evolution, a key requirement for reliable, efficient neural surrogates in scientific applications.
items.title: Beyond Compression: Training Latent Representations for Stable Long-Horizon Rollout in Neural Surrogate Solvers

items.summary: Existing point tracking models face a fundamental tradeoff: they can either track a sparse set of query points over long horizons, or track all points across only short clips. We introduce TrackEverything, a 3D point tracker that breaks this trade-off by representing videos as persistent 3D scene tracks in world coordinates. Grounded in the insight that videos are 2D projections of an underlying 3D world, TrackEverything decouples model complexity from video duration, allowing it to scale with unique physical scene geometry instead. Our approach introduces three key innovations. First, we employ a voxelization-based de-duplication mechanism at sliding-window boundaries to merge co-located tracks, preventing repeated observations of the same surface from redundantly accumulating. Second, we decompose tracking into an endpoint refiner that predicts each point's destination and static-versus-dynamic classification, followed by a lightweight trajectory refiner that decodes dense trajectories exclusively for dynamic points. Third, we propose 3D WAFT, replacing memory-prohibitive 4D correlation volumes with efficient feature sampling in the scene cloud. To the best of our knowledge, TrackEverything is the first 3D tracker capable of tracking all visible points across videos exceeding 1000 frames within 40 GB of GPU memory. On TAPVid-3D, TrackEverything outperforms all open-source all-frame dense 3D trackers by more than 20% APD on short clips, while remaining competitive with state-of-the-art sparse trackers on long sequences, despite tracking far more points.
items.title: TrackEverything: Long Horizon Dense Tracking via De-Duplicating 3D Scene Representations

items.summary: Textured Gaussians improve local appearance capacity, but assigning the same texture resolution to every primitive wastes storage on low-detail or weakly visible regions. We introduce AdaTex4D, an adaptive texture-capacity module for deformation-based 4D Gaussian Splatting. Each Gaussian carries packed RGBA triplanes whose two axes grow independently according to visibility normalized screen-space gradients and deformed local scales. Experiments on N3DV and PanopticSports show that AdaTex4D reduces texture storage by more than half while preserving reconstruction quality. Under fixed memory budgets, adaptive allocation also improves quality over uniform texture assignment and reduces overall model and peak memory. These results show that dynamic, anisotropic texture allocation provides a more efficient way to distribute local appearance capacity in 4D Gaussian representations.
items.title: ADATEX4D: adaptive texture capacity allocation for 4D gaussian splatting

items.summary: Detecting Design and Architecture Smells with LLM-Based and Agentic Strategies This repository contains the replication package for the study: How Context Shapes LLM-Based and Agentic Detection of Design and Architecture Smells The study evaluates how different context construction strategies affect the detection of design and architecture smells using Large Language Models (LLMs) and coding agents. We compare direct LLM invocation with predefined contexts against Mini-swe-agent-based repository exploration. items.summary: On a supplied real Euclidean two-plane, admitting both rotations and reflections gives the transport group O(2) = U(1) ⋊ Z₂, not an untwisted circle. We organize the resulting graph, face, refinement, and readout structures in one assumption-controlled framework. On a connected finite graph, tree gauge reduces the edge data to a simultaneous conjugacy class of free generators. Its determinant class lies in H¹(Γ; Z₂), while the phase is a crossed cocycle for the associated sign action. Admitting faces introduces additional path comparisons: their determinant defects obey a relative boundary law, and a rooted tetrahedral word gives an exact non-Abelian Bianchi identity whose phase sum is sign-twisted. Shared-edge and common-root data permit exact boundary cancellation under the stated disk refinements. Explicit pentagonal and hexagonal certificates include all five and fourteen triangulations, respectively, and two mixed 1–3, 2–2, 3–1 routes. Mismatched-edge and omitted-root controls distinguish invalid fusion, while a preserved reverse-order null control shows why equality of evaluated matrices is weaker than equality of free boundary words. A locally flat annulus retains a nontrivial noncontractible reflection holonomy. Finally, conjugacy data, one prepared direction, a complete endpoint frame, and a separately supplied complex-linear process representation have different identification power. The component graph-gauge, cohomological, lattice-Bianchi, and triangulation structures have established antecedents. The proposed contribution is their explicit finite integration with typed root, edge-sharing, and access contracts. No arbitrary-mesh or continuum invariance, higher gauge theory, quantum-state selection, winding lift, probability law, or empirical realization follows from the construction.

items.summary: Contactless palmprint recognition is attractive for mobile biometrics, yet how well a learned representation transfers between acquisition settings is rarely measured. Using CompNet - a compact network of learnable Gabor filters and competitive coding — we apply one unified protocol to two contrasting databases: the constrained near-infrared IITD and the unconstrained smartphone SMPD. Within each, CompNet reaches 98.70% Rank-1 accuracy at an equal-error rate below 1.4%. Across databases the transfer is asymmetric: mobile-trained features generalize to controlled data (91.10%), whereas the reverse collapses (40.03%), so generalization flows from harder to easier domains.
items.title: Contactless palmprint identification using CompNet on the IITD and SMPD databases

items.summary: Artifact accompanying a manuscript under double-blind review . Author information is withheld until publication; a later version of this record will carry it, and the concept DOI is stable across versions. What this is. When two unlabelled subgroups of documents are compared by embedding similarity across languages, countries, corpora or periods, and the difference is read as evidence about those sources, no accuracy figure certifies that reading. within_language_baseline.py supplies the missing baseline: it measures the same subgroup contrast inside a single source, where no across-source relation can enter, and reports the residual with a bootstrap interval and an equivalence verdict against a margin declared in advance. The tool has no dependency on the accompanying study and runs on any corpus with three columns ( text , group , source ). It carries its own injection tests ( --selftest ). The bootstrap resamples documents rather than pairs and excludes duplicate draws of the same document from within-source pairs. Also included: the 36 frozen anchor correspondences used as the gold standard, the per-encoder CJK retrieval evaluation, the measured within-language and cross-country genre gaps, the equivalence intervals, an append-only correction record for the non-analytic genealogy fields of the frozen anchors, and anonymised review copies of the post hoc centring protocols and of the departure record. MANIFEST.sha256 covers every deposited file except itself.
items.title: Replication artifact for "Auditing Cross-Lingual Statutory Similarity Contrasts: Centring Choices and Within-Language Baselines"

items.summary: Anonymised dataset and analysis code supporting the article "When security becomes a barrier: digital caregivers and rating hijacking in a national mHealth application" (revised submission, International Journal of Medical Informatics). The package contains 2,943 anonymised Google Play reviews of Türkiye's national appointment application (MHRS) posted between 1 January and 1 April 2026, sentiment labels from a researcher-reviewed rule-based pipeline (distributed in duygu_siniflandirma.py), second-coder reliability files, and typology codes for 466 sentiment–rating discordant cases. Coverage note: the retrieved stream is complete across star levels only on 23 February–7 March and 31 March–1 April; elsewhere it is almost exclusively five-star, the signature of relevance-ordered retrieval — see README.md and the article's Appendix A.6. Version 1.2 adds this coverage audit and rev_R1_analyses.py, which reproduces every statistic in the revised manuscript; analiz_kodu.py is retained as the record of the original submission. Usernames and personally identifying information were removed prior to deposit.
items.title: Replication data and code for: When security becomes a barrier: digital caregivers and rating hijacking in a national mHealth application

items.summary: Modern astrophysical research requires the integration of rapidly expanding scientific literature, heterogeneous observational data, and increasingly complex physical models. We introduce AstroGenesis (https://astrogenai.com), a domain-specific multi-agent AI framework that integrates literature retrieval, multiwavelength data access and analysis, theoretical modeling, and research ideation within a unified research environment.The current implementation focuses on blazar research, with specialized agents coordinated by a Supervisor Agent and Planner/Replanner architecture. These agents provide capabilities for retrieving and synthesizing literature, accessing and analyzing multiwavelength observations, performing physical modeling, and identifying research directions. A central component is the Theoretical Modeling Agent, which uses pretrained neural-network surrogate models to enable efficient broadband and multimessenger modeling through natural-language interaction. The framework provides natural-language access to science-ready multiwavelength observational data and retrieval-grounded literature through a multi-stage retrieval and ranking pipeline. The literature-retrieval system was evaluated using two benchmarks: a single-paper benchmark, in which each question targets one publication, and a multi-paper benchmark, in which questions may require evidence from several publications. At least one relevant publication was retrieved among the top five results for 76.6% of the single-paper questions and 79.2% of the multi-paper questions. Representative workflows demonstrate how literature, observational data, physical modeling, and hypothesis generation can be combined within traceable analyses. The framework is extensible to additional astrophysical domains, with the goal of streamlining research workflows and enabling efficient, connected, and reproducible scientific investigations.
items.title: AstroGenesis: A Domain-Specific Multi-Agent AI for Astrophysical Research

items.summary: Blockchain and artificial intelligence (AI) are converging into a single infrastructural layer for securing data sharing, model integrity, and autonomous decision-making across distributed systems. This paper presents a meta-synthesis that draws together four constituent studies covering adversarial machine learning, AI-powered anomaly detection in cloud environments, automated vulnerability patching by multi-agent large language model (LLM) pipelines, and the broader landscape of securing AI systems across their lifecycle and situates their findings within the emerging literature on blockchain-enabled AI and autonomous AI agents. Each constituent study addresses a distinct point of failure in modern AI-driven security operations: the integrity of training data and model behavior, the reliability of real-time monitoring, and the trustworthiness of automated code remediation. We argue that blockchain's properties of immutability, decentralized consensus, and verifiable provenance directly address a gap common to all three: the difficulty of establishing trust in data, models, and autonomous agents that operate without a central authority. Building on real-world research on blockchain-secured data sharing, federated learning, and multi-agent coordination, we propose a layered reference architecture that couples adversarially hardened models, blockchain-anchored data provenance, AI-driven anomaly detection, and smart-contract-governed multi-agent remediation. We conclude by identifying open problems in scalability, privacy-transparency trade-offs, and the governance of autonomous agents that must be resolved before such integrated systems can be trusted in production-critical environments.
items.title: Blockchain-Enabled Artificial Intelligence and AI Agents for Secure Data Sharing and Cybersecurity Applications

items.summary: We address the inverse problem of reconstructing the initial temperature distribution in a one-dimensional non-homogeneous heat equation with Dirichlet boundary conditions from a finite number of pointwise-in-time measurements at a single spatial location. We propose an explicit approximation scheme that incorporates the source term and utilizes a refined sequence of measurement times. Unlike previous approaches that often rely on exponentially growing observation times, our chosen time sequence allows for efficient recovery within a fixed time horizon. We establish algebraic convergence rates under suitable regularity assumptions on the initial data and the forcing, and we validate the theoretical sharpness with numerical experiments for varying numbers of measurements.
items.title: Reconstruction of the Initial Condition for a Non-Homogeneous Heat Equation from Finite Measurements

items.summary: High-order differential operators and nonlinear coupling make it challenging to construct conservative and energy-stable schemes for coupled gradient-flow systems. We present GradAgent, a knowledge-guided multi-agent system that coordinates three agents across model analysis, algorithm design and proofs, and numerical implementation and validation. Independent audits strengthen reliability by uncovering mathematical errors and proof gaps, guiding revisions, and maintaining consistency across stages. In Reconstruction Mode, GradAgent reconstructs 20 published studies and organizes audited knowledge in an extensible knowledge graph (KG), GradAgent-KG, linking model structures, discretization strategies and proofs, implementations, and numerical evidence. In Design Mode, the agents assess the applicability of retrieved knowledge and develop new schemes informed by relevant discretization strategies. Applied to the fully coupled multicomponent vesicle phase-field-fluid model, GradAgent yields three first-order and three second-order schemes across three algorithmic families, including four linear, decoupled schemes. Under stated assumptions, all six schemes conserve membrane component mass and vesicle volume and dissipate their respective temporally discrete energies unconditionally. Comparisons with and without GradAgent-KG show that it promotes diversity in structure-preserving scheme design for this target model. Numerical tests confirm second-order spatial accuracy, the expected temporal orders, conservation, and temporally discrete energy dissipation, while three-dimensional shear-flow simulations agree qualitatively with experiments. These results demonstrate GradAgent's ability to combine reusable knowledge, coordinated reasoning, and independent auditing to develop and validate structure-preserving algorithms for complex coupled systems.
items.title: GradAgent: A Knowledge-Guided Multi-Agent System for Structure-Preserving Gradient-Flow Computation with an Application to Multicomponent Vesicle Dynamics

items.summary: The fidelity of image reconstruction from projections in linear inverse problems, such as tomography, is critically dependent on the synergistic interaction between frequency-domain filtering and spatial-domain interpolation. However, a physical model that can quantitatively describe how these two components cascade interact in the frequency domain and ultimately determine image quality is still lacking to this day. Here, we introduce a unified frequency-domain model that conceptualizes the combined effect of filtering and interpolation in the filtered backprojection (FBP) algorithm as a cascaded modulation process. This model demonstrates that the effective reconstruction spectrum is determined by the original projection data being sequentially modulated by the frequency responses of the filter and the interpolation kernel. Comprehensive numerical simulations and synchrotron radiation CT experiments validate the model, confirming its power to explain the performance hierarchy of classical filter-interpolation pairs under both ideal and noisy conditions. The model successfully predicts key performance characteristics, including spatial resolution and structural fidelity, thereby elucidating the physical principles behind the efficacy of specific combinations. This work establishes a generalizable theoretical foundation for analyzing cascaded systems in linear inverse problems, moving the practice of algorithm selection in computational imaging from empiricism to a principled, physics-based paradigm.
items.title: A Unified Frequency-Domain Model for Cascaded Filter-Interpolation Modulation in Tomographic Reconstruction

items.summary: Minimal strings offer two ways to study quantum surfaces: through a spectral curve or through a differential equation. We ask how much of the quantum equation can be recovered once the classical curve and its motion with the background are known. Our starting point is the resolvent of a scalar differential operator. We require its one-boundary integral to have poles only at branch points, with the resulting differential regular at infinity. These conditions give a finite reconstruction procedure at each genus. When the branch points are simple and their energy values move, we prove that the quantum corrections are unique whenever the procedure is consistent. A specified string equation provides a solution if its trace primitive satisfies the same analytic conditions. The scalar construction also leads to amplitudes with several boundaries. We introduce the method through pure gravity and Ising, then explore higher-order, dual and nonunitary models. Higher-Airy examples connect the calculation to $r$-spin theory on a degenerate locus that requires a separate treatment of the inverse problem.
items.title: Resolvent reconstruction of minimal strings beyond KdV

items.summary: Abstract   The Universal Research System with Reverse Itinerary (SUII) is a retrospective analytical methodology designed to reconstruct, in a traceable and auditable manner, the probable pathway leading from an initial problem or question to a completed scientific product. This manual brings together the universal prompt, a mandatory common core, ten core modules—including bibliographic analysis (SUII-B)—and five specialised extensions: journalistic and opinion texts (SUII-P), audiovisual or audio documents (SUII-AV), legislation and regulatory documents (SUII-L), case law and judicial decisions (SUII-J), and critical appraisal of scientific articles (SUII-LC). Each module guides the extraction of locatable traces, classification of the epistemic status of claims, and construction of matrices linking evidence, inference, confidence, alternatives, and required verification. The method separates retrospective reconstruction from the prospective generation of hypotheses and requires rival explanations whenever the evidence does not support a unique conclusion. It also incorporates procedures for methodological auditing, version comparison, conceptual genealogy, peer review, algorithmic-bias assessment, external validation, and teaching. SUII is not intended to recover the authors’ actual psychological history or to replace validated tools for methodological appraisal, risk-of-bias assessment, or evaluation of certainty of evidence. Its application requires version-controlled corpora, decision logs, retention of prompts and outputs, source verification, and mandatory human oversight. When the available traces are insufficient, the appropriate result is “not determinable.” The manual provides practical criteria for selecting, combining, and quality-controlling the modules according to the product under analysis and the research objective, while maintaining explicit boundaries between documented evidence, reasoned inference, speculation, and unresolved uncertainty.   Resumen   El Sistema Universal de Investigación con Itinerario Inverso (SUII) es una metodología de análisis retrospectivo orientada a reconstruir , de forma trazable y auditable, el itinerario probable que conduce desde un problema o pregunta inicial hasta un producto científico finalizado . Este manual reúne el prompt universal, un núcleo común obligatorio , diez módulos nucleares y cinco extensiones especializadas : análisis bibliográfico (SUII-B), textos periodísticos y de opinión (SUII-P), documentos audiovisuales o sonoros (SUII-AV), legislación y normativa (SUII-L), jurisprudencia y sentencias (SUII-J), y lectura crítica de artículos científicos (SUII-LC). Cada módulo guía la extracción de huellas localizables , la clasificación del estado epistemológico de las afirmaciones y la construcción de matrices que relacionan evidencia , inferencia , confianza, alternativas y comprobaciones necesarias . El método separa la reconstrucción retrospectiva de la generación prospectiva de hipótesis y exige formular explicaciones rivales cuando la evidencia no permite una conclusión única . items.summary: Finite-domain normalized spatial measurements combine an incident field, geometric support, local response, and channel weighting. These operations can break an otherwise separable response, so accurate single-axis calibration alone does not establish separability of a multidimensional measurement. We represent normalized readouts as channel-weight expectations under a parameter-dependent effective measure. For fixed reception and channel operators, local sensitivity is the covariance between the channel weight and the source score. This representation distinguishes axis separability, parameter mixing, and local recoverability, and applies at the appropriate detector level to continuous-electrode position-sensitive detectors, Shack--Hartmann and pyramid wavefront sensors, back-focal-plane split detection, and finite pixel arrays. A quadrant photodetector (QPD) provides an analytically tractable case. Starting from the complete two-dimensional power integrals, we identify the spatial-moment origin of its lowest-order cross term. Axis calibration and system symmetry then constrain the inverse map, giving Axis-Anchored Cross-Residual Inversion (ACRI). Numerical tests of this QPD realization support the sensitivity relations and show that the constrained cross correction substantially reduces the off-axis bias retained by single-axis inversion. The results illustrate how the general measurement representation guides inverse construction, with performance bounded by the working domain, calibration state, and preserved symmetries.
items.title: Breakdown of Axis Separability and Structured Inversion in Finite-Domain Normalized Position Measurements: A Quadrant Photodetector Case Study

items.summary: One-way functions exist if and only if some efficiently samplable process produces more than logarithmic computational entropy on average, for infinitely many input lengths. We make this precise. For a polynomial-time samplable distribution D on pairs (x, y), the computational entropy production of a pair is σ = log D(x, y) + pK^t(y) + pK^t(x | y), where pK^t is the probabilistic time-bounded Kolmogorov complexity as defined by Hirahara, Ilango, Lu, Nanashima and Oliveira (2023, HILNO below) following Goldberg, Kabanets, Lu and Oliveira (2022): the log-probability the process assigns to the pair, against the length of a bounded observer's shortest fast description of it, output first, then input given output. We prove unconditionally that E_D[2^{−σ}] lies between an inverse polynomial and a polynomial in n and that E_D[σ] ≥ −O(log n): a time-bounded fluctuation inequality and a computational second law. We show that, up to a polynomial and outside a 1/n slice of outputs, σ is small on a pair exactly when an efficient sampler, given the output, recovers the input with about the right odds, HILNO's universal sampler serving as the witness: dissipation, in this sense, is the hardness of running the process backward. The equivalence in the first sentence is HILNO's duality restated in these terms, for infinitely-often one-way functions and at every polynomial time bound. For the antisymmetric Zurek defect, one-way functions force superpolynomial exponential moments, and bounded moments sit between NP ⊆ BPP and the non-existence of one-way functions; whether the lower arrow reverses is left open, with a conditional relativization barrier on that arrow and oracle evidence on the other. Physics is the frame, not the subject.
items.title: One-way functions are computational entropy production

items.summary: Diffusion models are powerful priors for linear inverse problems, but the reference guidance methods, Diffusion Posterior Sampling (DPS) and Pseudoinverse-Guided Diffusion Models ($Π$GDM), rely on scalar hyperparameters tuned per task, usually against the ground truth. We introduce FB-GDM, a fully-Bayesian guided diffusion method that removes this calibration step. Starting from the Gaussian approximation of $Π$GDM, we derive a closed-form conditional score that depends on two precision parameters (inverse variances), one associated with the denoising approximation and one with the observation likelihood, and treat them as latent variables inferred by variational inference at each reverse step. A separable factorization makes each update scale linearly with the number of pixels, so the inference stays tractable at full image resolution, at a cost comparable to one $Π$GDM run. FB-GDM requires neither the noise level nor the ground truth: its only inputs are the observation and the forward operator. Experiments on CelebA-HQ inverse problems establish two results. (i) The precision parameters, inferred from the observation alone, allow FB-GDM to outperform $Π$GDM at its nominal setting, even when the latter is given the true noise level, by up to 14 dB depending on the operator, and to match the ground-truth-calibrated $Π$GDM oracle within 0.1 dB. (ii) FB-GDM is robust when the forward operator, the noise level, or the image distribution changes: it stays close to a per-problem $Π$GDM oracle throughout and does not exhibit the hallucinations observed with DPS, whereas DPS substantially degrades at a fixed scale and $Π$GDM stays competitive only if it is re-tuned against the ground truth for each new problem. When the prior is applied to images outside its training set, this re-balancing between data and prior keeps FB-GDM faithful where a fixed face-prior guidance can otherwise hallucinate.

items.summary: Textured Gaussians improve local appearance capacity, but assigning the same texture resolution to every primitive wastes storage on low-detail or weakly visible regions. We introduce AdaTex4D, an adaptive texture-capacity module for deformation-based 4D Gaussian Splatting. Each Gaussian carries packed RGBA triplanes whose two axes grow independently according to visibility normalized screen-space gradients and deformed local scales. Experiments on N3DV and PanopticSports show that AdaTex4D reduces texture storage by more than half while preserving reconstruction quality. Under fixed memory budgets, adaptive allocation also improves quality over uniform texture assignment and reduces overall model and peak memory. These results show that dynamic, anisotropic texture allocation provides a more efficient way to distribute local appearance capacity in 4D Gaussian representations.
items.title: ADATEX4D: adaptive texture capacity allocation for 4D gaussian splatting

items.summary: This corrected data and reproducibility archive supports the manuscript “Human protein complex interfaces reveal candidate assembly roles for initiator methionine excision.” It asks which human protein N-terminal positions engage assembly partners and whether their interface environments nominate specific roles for methionine removal. The archive combines a human structural census with terminal-boundary sensitivity analyses, evidence-qualified comparisons and partner-resolved proteasome geometry. Its central biological message is that the possible importance of methionine removal depends not only on sequence, but also on which partner an N-terminal position encounters in a particular assembly context. The complete contract for 12 tasks across three domains — astrophysics (simulated and real Stokes inversion, PLAsTiCC light-curve classification), high-energy physics (top-quark tagging, HiggsML uncertainty quantification, LHC Olympics anomaly detection, DarkMachines anomaly detection), and neuroscience (ABIDE multi-site diagnosis and age prediction, resting-state BOLD HRF deconvolution, neural-mass model family classification, parameter recovery, and digital twins). Per task: the agent-facing task statement, the scoring definition, the grader, per-file SHA-256 checksums, a literature index citing sources by DOI, baseline and expert reference solutions, and dataset-generation code where the payload is synthetic. Leaderboards and the per-run report used for the reported results, plus the campaign script that records the exact model, agent, sandbox, reasoning effort, and budget limits behind them. WHAT IT DOES NOT CONTAIN Dataset payloads are not in this archive. They are published as a companion dataset record, https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.22960135, as one archive per task, each unpacking at this repository's root. Every task ships per-file SHA-256 checksums so any copy can be verified byte-for-byte. Without the payloads the harness can be inspected and extended, but tasks cannot be executed or scored. All arrays are produced by scripts/evaluate.py and scripts/posterior_sampling.py in the evaluating-generative-models code repository, applied to trained checkpoints of the learned methods. The exact commands are documented in notebooks/README.md . notebooks_executed/ — executed analysis notebooks benchmark1_synthetic_executed.ipynb - end-to-end synthetic benchmark (Section 5; Table 1; Figures 1, 3, 4, 5). Reads the arrays under  benchmark2/ and produces every Benchmark II figure and table in the paper. The copies in this deposit are the same notebooks executed once against the data files included here, with the resulting figures and tables embedded as outputs. For re-execution from data: clone the evaluating-generative-models code repository, follow its installation instructions in README.md , place the contents of this deposit's benchmark2/ directory under data/benchmark2/ (documented in notebooks/README.md ), and run the cleared notebooks under notebooks/ . Outputs should match the executed notebooks included here. For full regeneration from checkpoints: requires the dileptonic ttbar neutrino regression dataset (Raine et al., 2023) and trained model checkpoints produced by scripts/train.py . It includes candidate/native IAE, ISE, MAE and MSE, paired increments, M/L, the three original windows, comparison bands, complete result tables and accounting identities. No new trajectories were generated for this metric analysis. The preserved CCE1 archive supplies the baseline and amplitude/noise studies: three tank amplitudes under two solvers and 120 TEP histories from three severities, ten paired measurement-noise seed groups and four profiles. Analysis code, fixed specifications, selected-input hashes, numerical results and execution records remain unchanged; only release documentation and administrative manifests were updated. Original CCE1 provenance is retained. Shared histories, multiple metrics/windows and solver refinements are not independent validation samples. items.summary: Blockchain and artificial intelligence (AI) are converging into a single infrastructural layer for securing data sharing, model integrity, and autonomous decision-making across distributed systems. This paper presents a meta-synthesis that draws together four constituent studies covering adversarial machine learning, AI-powered anomaly detection in cloud environments, automated vulnerability patching by multi-agent large language model (LLM) pipelines, and the broader landscape of securing AI systems across their lifecycle and situates their findings within the emerging literature on blockchain-enabled AI and autonomous AI agents. Each constituent study addresses a distinct point of failure in modern AI-driven security operations: the integrity of training data and model behavior, the reliability of real-time monitoring, and the trustworthiness of automated code remediation. We argue that blockchain's properties of immutability, decentralized consensus, and verifiable provenance directly address a gap common to all three: the difficulty of establishing trust in data, models, and autonomous agents that operate without a central authority. Building on real-world research on blockchain-secured data sharing, federated learning, and multi-agent coordination, we propose a layered reference architecture that couples adversarially hardened models, blockchain-anchored data provenance, AI-driven anomaly detection, and smart-contract-governed multi-agent remediation. We conclude by identifying open problems in scalability, privacy-transparency trade-offs, and the governance of autonomous agents that must be resolved before such integrated systems can be trusted in production-critical environments.
items.title: Blockchain-Enabled Artificial Intelligence and AI Agents for Secure Data Sharing and Cybersecurity Applications

items.summary: This replication package accompanies the revised manuscript “Authority–Inference Separation in Agentic Finance: Intent-Bound Control, EVM Enforcement, and Replayable Assurance” (Systems manuscript systems-4566123). It provides the deterministic AIS prototype, 48 original fixtures, separate 36-case mechanism-ablation and 24-case external-gateway evaluations, randomized property tests, concurrency and semantic-boundary cases, live-model outputs, a Solidity EVM enforcement prototype with local-chain results, and a bounded public-ledger observability dataset with source manifest and quality notes. The README gives reproducibility instructions and distinct evaluation denominators. These research prototypes are not production controls, a smart-contract security audit, or estimates of real-world attack prevalence. items.summary: We present Underwater C$^{3}$-JEPA (cross-view, control-conditioned, context-extended), an object-centric multi-view predictive world model for near-field heavy-load underwater ROV salvage. Without contact sensors, it predicts in latent space how the task-object state evolves through contact interaction and under the hydrodynamic lag of the vehicle, from synchronized multi-view RGB observations and vehicle control signals. C$^{3}$-JEPA encodes multi-camera observations into task-object and context tokens, fuses cross-camera evidence through held-out-view attention, and directly predicts future states conditioned on control. Weak binding anchors the target and gripper at low annotation cost, while SIGReg sharpens the geometric representation. Experiments show that the learned representation transfers substantially more task-relevant information to downstream probes than a reconstruction-free latent baseline, while keeping the predictor lightweight. The resulting predictive interface supports model-predictive-control (MPC) candidate evaluation and imagined-rollout behavior-agent training. Validation on real underwater video shows the same architecture recovering a withheld camera's object state and staying ahead of persistence, so the recipe transfers beyond simulation.
items.title: Underwater C3-JEPA: An Object-Centric Cross-View World Model for ROV Salvage

items.summary: This deposit contains the data files and pre-executed analysis notebooks that accompany the paper Evaluating Multimodal Inverse Problems: A Protocol for Per-Event and Population-Level Fidelity (currently under review at ICLR 2027). It is the supplementary artifact to the evaluating-generative-models code repository: anonymous.4open.science/r/evaluating-generative-models-C559/ The repository contains the source code, configurations, and notebooks (with outputs cleared); this Zenodo deposit contains the precomputed arrays the notebooks read and the same notebooks with all figures and tables embedded. Contents benchmark2/ — precomputed arrays for the dileptonic top-quark benchmark Each .npz file collects per-event quantities for all four methods evaluated in Section 6 of the paper: the analytic solver, the MSE-trained transformer regression, the MMD-regularised transformer regression, the discrete normalising flow, and the continuous normalising flow. evaluation_without_nlls.npz - per-event point predictions and posterior summaries used for the headline metrics (CRPS, RMSE, spectrum fidelity) of Tables 2 and 8. evaluation_with_nlls.npz - the same arrays augmented with per-event log-likelihoods, used as nonconformity scores for the conformal calibration of Section 4.3 / appendix D.10. posteriors_without_nlls.npz - dense posterior samples (50000 per event for a 150-event subset) used for the per-event posterior figures of Figure 2(a) and Figure 8. posteriors_with_nlls.npz - dense posterior samples (20000 per event for a 40-event subset) with NLLs for all samples. analytic_tops.npy - reconstructed top-quark four-vectors from the analytic solver baseline. seed_stability.npz - Multiple discrete flow model samples for Benchmark II robustness analysis (Table 7). multiseed_w_cfm.npz - Multiple evaluations for fluctuation studies across training seeds. All arrays are produced by scripts/evaluate.py and scripts/posterior_sampling.py in the evaluating-generative-models code repository, applied to trained checkpoints of the learned methods. The exact commands are documented in notebooks/README.md . notebooks_executed/ — executed analysis notebooks benchmark1_synthetic_executed.ipynb - end-to-end synthetic benchmark (Section 5; Table 1; Figures 1, 3, 4, 5). Self-contained: generates data, trains the four models (regression MLP, heteroscedastic regression, mixture density network, normalising flow), computes all metrics, produces all figures. benchmark2_plotting_executed.ipynb - physics benchmark (Section 6; Tables 2, 7 and 8; Figures 2, 6, 7, 8, 9). Reads the arrays under  benchmark2/ and produces every Benchmark II figure and table in the paper. Both notebooks are also present in the code repository with cleared outputs so they are diff-friendly under version control. The copies in this deposit are the same notebooks executed once against the data files included here, with the resulting figures and tables embedded as outputs. How to use For viewing only: open the notebooks under notebooks_executed/ in any Jupyter viewer (including GitHub's renderer and nbviewer ). All figures are embedded. No installation required. For re-execution from data: clone the evaluating-generative-models code repository, follow its installation instructions in README.md , place the contents of this deposit's benchmark2/ directory under data/benchmark2/ (documented in notebooks/README.md ), and run the cleared notebooks under notebooks/ . Outputs should match the executed notebooks included here. For full regeneration from checkpoints: requires the dileptonic ttbar neutrino regression dataset (Raine et al., 2023) and trained model checkpoints produced by scripts/train.py . See the code repository's README.md for the full pipeline. Provenance and dependencies The arrays were generated with the evaluating-generative-models codebase (MIT License) (commit hash to be added at de-anonymization) using the dileptonic ttbar neutrino regression dataset by Rai

items.summary: Replication package for the manuscript What AI Coding Agents Claim and What We Can Measure: Non-Functional Requirement Claims, Extraction Validity, and Intent–Outcome Consistency in Agent-Authored Pull Requests , prepared for submission to Empirical Software Engineering (special issue: Agentic Software Engineering). Contents: the IntentValidator pipeline source snapshot and run configurations; the per-claim datasets of the canonical agent run, of the all-repository human comparison cohort (with its protocol, draw listings and order of events) and of the superseded first human cohort, plus the re-runs that document the effect of the pipeline's timeouts; the 186-pattern NFR claim catalog, boilerplate-stripping rules and the full match table; the extraction-validity ladder and regression scripts; the manual-validation kit (stratified samples, rubric, blind labelling tool, both human raters' sheets with untouched exports and SHA-256 sums, three disclosed LLM annotation passes with per-item rationales and provenance, the LLM-judge sensitivity, the adjudication queue, a recall probe of unflagged pull requests with blind sheets and a disclosed LLM screen, and a kit for a rater from outside the author team); the consistency analysis on the human-validated claims, the Maintainability-Index floor sensitivity and the all-language cross-check of the index against independent Halstead implementations (per-claim results); every analysis script that regenerates the manuscript's numbers and figures; and a checksum manifest of every file with named reproduction checks. The archive carries the replication tree only; the manuscript itself is not included. The AIDev dataset itself is not redistributed; obtain it from its own Zenodo record (10.5281/zenodo.16919272). The 25 September 2026 audit revision adds explicit sampling and interpretation limitations, corrected stratification of diagnostic agreement intervals, clarified nominal instrument coverage, and reproducibility notes. Original human labels and canonical claim verdicts are preserved; catalogue label/rubric conflicts remain for human reassessment. See replication/09-paper/emse-2026/replication/REVIEW-NOTES-2026-09-25.md.
items.title: Replication package: What AI Coding Agents Claim and What We Can Measure (IntentValidator, NFR claim catalog, two-rater manual validation)

items.summary: This record provides reproducibility materials supporting the manuscript “Actual-use verification and lineage-resolved fidelity in scientific AI”. The study evaluates scientific-AI fidelity by distinguishing assigned scientific objects, realized scientific objects, lineage or pathway fidelity, terminal scientific fidelity and claim boundaries.   The archive contains detailed evidence registries, comparison specifications, provenance and audit records, structured source records, manuscript source materials, display assets, and code for assembling and rendering the supplied publication materials. It also preserves the available historical CoralTemp/Coral Reef Watch daily-classification source excerpt used in the documented evidence chain.   The released materials support inspection of the reported evidence, scientific-object assignments, realized-use verification, lineage-resolved comparisons and presentation-level reproduction. They do not constitute a complete executable end-to-end reproduction of all scientific analyses. Complete raw-input and terminal-reference payloads, full benchmark execution and scoring pipelines, original scientific figure-generation programs and the original pinned scientific execution environments are not included. Public upstream scientific products and their provenance are documented in the manuscript and archive.   The archive should therefore be interpreted as a provenance-rich reproducibility and audit package rather than as a general benchmark of scientific-AI accuracy or reliability.
items.title: Reproducibility materials for "Actual-use verification and lineage-resolved fidelity in scientific AI"

items.summary: This record contains the public reproducibility package supporting the study “Persistent spatial organization and period-dependent associations in Beijing’s surface thermal–moisture environment”. The package includes the model-ready analytical dataset, temporal-screening and provenance records, cross-validation folds, model parameters and random-seed records, formal scripts for pooled and period-specific XGBoost–SHAP analyses, GeoDetector analysis, stored model outputs, quality-control and checksum records, and selected figure-source materials. The study comprises seven quality-controlled summer observation periods: 2000, 2004, 2005, 2009, 2010, 2016, and 2019. The primary reproducibility target of this package is the reported statistical analysis beginning from the archived ModelReady dataset. Production scripts preserve the original execution paths used during the formal analysis; users reproducing the analyses should update input and output paths to their local repository location. Upstream geospatial preprocessing scripts are retained for methodological provenance and may require the original third-party source products and local GIS configuration. Original Landsat, GLC_FCS30D, WorldPop, and Copernicus DEM source archives are not redistributed in this record and should be obtained from their respective providers. Detailed package structure, provenance, execution scope, and reproducibility notes are provided in the included README. Source code created by the authors is released under the MIT License. Third-party and derived source materials remain subject to the terms of their original providers and are not relicensed by this record.
